claims.claim: Modernity has traditionally been presented as the age when artifacts supplant nature and destroy the natural environment, which is the process of de-naturalization, but Hannah Arendt questioned this view by arguing that a process of re-naturalization has been taking place to the detriment of the human world.
claims.supporting_excerpt: Modernity, in philosophical and sociological literature, has “traditionally” been presented as the age when artifacts supplant nature and destroy the originally given natural environment. The process of modernization, from this point of view, is the process of de-naturalization . This widely shared conviction has ba - sically been questioned by Hannah Arendt. During the centuries of modern age, in the detriment of the commonly created and uphold human world, process of re-naturalization  has been taking place, Arendt argues.

claims.claim: Arendt was primarily worried not about the dominance of technology, but about the threat of re-naturalization, which in terms of political philosophy embodies the victory of natural necessity over liberty.
claims.supporting_excerpt: She was worrying, first of all, not about the dominance of technology but the threat of re-naturalization (Villa 1996: 201) which, transposing it to the terms of political philosophy, for her, embodied the victory of natural necessity over liberty.

definitions.definition: The process where artifacts supplant nature and destroy the originally given natural environment.
A process taking place during the modern age to the detriment of the commonly created and upheld human world, enhanced by technology and embodying the victory of natural necessity over liberty.

distinctions.distinction: The Arendtian critique of modernity takes a difference between the notions of Earth and world.

must_not_be_lost: Arendt's framing of the natural and artificial places the problem within two narratives: cultural criticism and political philosophy.
The ecological connotations of the natural-artificial dichotomy in The Human Condition were subordinated to the requirements of her political philosophy.
parsed.segment_function: Introduction, contextual background, and statement of the paper's hypothesis regarding Hannah Arendt's interpretation of the natural and artificial in The Human Condition.
unresolved_context: Specific details of how Heidegger's philosophy influenced Arendt's distinction between Earth and world beyond the stated text.
